evals.prompt: Upgrade ScannerV7.c from Scandit Linux SDK 7.4 to 8.6.
evals.expected_output: Reads references/migration.md, detects 7.x from the code, applies the 7 → 8 table in the file, lists behaviour changes between 7.4 and 8.6 as judgment calls, and summarizes. Judge API-absence assertions against code blocks / written files only; prose may name old APIs.

assertions.text: The installed version is identified as 7.x (from the code or by asking) and the 7 → 8 path is applied
In the code, sc_barcode_scanner_new_with_settings is replaced by sc_barcode_scanner_new( followed by sc_barcode_scanner_apply_settings(
The ScContextStatus from sc_barcode_scanner_apply_settings is checked and freed with sc_context_status_free( (by value)

In the code, sc_barcode_scanner_settings_set_max_number_of_codes_per_frame is replaced by sc_barcode_scanner_settings_set_multi_scan_enabled( + sc_barcode_scanner_settings_set_max_num_locations_to_process_per_frame( with 4
In the code, result.status.flag is compared with SC_RECOGNITION_CONTEXT_STATUS_SUCCESS (not result.status)
In the code, sc_context_status_flag_get_message is replaced by sc_byte_array_get_string(result.status.message)
sc_process_frame_result_free( is called on every process_frame result
In the code, SC_SYMBOLOGY_RM4SCC is replaced by SC_SYMBOLOGY_ROYAL_MAIL_4STATE
The answer mentions that multi-scan needs the "tracking" license feature
The summary lists behaviour changes as judgment calls (e.g. 8.5 Code 128 minimum symbol count 4, tighter Code 39), not as renames
The answer says to replace scanditsdk.py / reinstall the .deb from the same new package and rebuild
The license-key placeholder/constant is preserved (no key read from the environment)

evals.prompt: We still run ScannerV5.c on SDK 5.x and have to move to 8.6 for a new device. Migrate it.
evals.expected_output: Detects 5.x, applies 5.x → 7.0 then 7 → 8 in order (Linux skipped 6.x): parser renames, EAN13_UPCA, no code caching, HIGH_EFFORT instead of the single-frame preset, ScByteArray instead of ScData, plane API instead of memory size, scanner creation and statuses for 8.x; mentions glibc. Judge API-absence assertions against code blocks / written files only; prose may name old APIs.

assertions.text: The answer applies 5.x → 7.0 first and then 7 → 8 (and mentions there is no Linux 6.x)
In the code, #include <Scandit/Parser/SpParser.h> becomes #include <Scandit/ScParser.h> and sp_parser_* / SpParser* become sc_parser_* / ScParser*
In the code, sc_parser_new_with_context( takes an ScContextStatus * as last argument (or NULL)
In the code, SC_SYMBOLOGY_EAN13 and SC_SYMBOLOGY_UPCA are replaced by SC_SYMBOLOGY_EAN13_UPCA
In the code, sc_barcode_scanner_settings_set_code_caching_duration is removed
In the code, SC_PRESET_ENABLE_SINGLE_FRAME_MODE is replaced by SC_PRESET_HIGH_EFFORT
In the code, ScData / sc_data_free / .c_str / .length are replaced by ScByteArray accessors (sc_byte_array_get_string / sc_byte_array_get_data / sc_byte_array_get_size)
In the code, sc_image_description_set_memory_size is removed and sc_image_description_set_plane_row_bytes( is set
In the code, the scanner is created with sc_barcode_scanner_new( + sc_barcode_scanner_apply_settings(
The answer mentions the newer glibc requirement for 7.0 and later
The answer suggests creating the context and scanner once instead of per image (or keeps the structure and notes it as a judgment call)

evals.prompt: We load settings_v7.json with sc_barcode_scanner_settings_new_from_json. After updating to 8.6 we only get one code per frame. Fix the file.
evals.expected_output: maxNumberOfCodesPerFrame is silently ignored in 8.x → multiScanEnabled + maxNumLocationsToProcessPerFrame; codeCachingDuration and focusMode removed; rm4scc → royal-mail-4state; data-matrix extensions replace defaults (add strip_leading_fnc1); check with as_json.

assertions.text: The answer says maxNumberOfCodesPerFrame is silently ignored in 8.x
The fixed JSON contains "multiScanEnabled": true and "maxNumLocationsToProcessPerFrame": 3
The fixed JSON does NOT contain maxNumberOfCodesPerFrame, codeCachingDuration or focusMode
"rm4scc" is replaced by "royal-mail-4state" (or the answer notes rm4scc is still accepted as input but royal-mail-4state is current)
The answer mentions that the data-matrix extensions array replaces the default extensions (strip_leading_fnc1)
The answer recommends comparing with sc_barcode_scanner_settings_as_json(
The answer mentions the "tracking" license feature for multi-scan

evals.prompt: ScannerWrapper.c implements our ScannerWrapper.h API on SDK 7.6. 14 call sites use that header. Port the implementation to 8.6.
evals.expected_output: Keeps ScannerWrapper.h unchanged (compatibility layer) and changes only the Scandit calls in ScannerWrapper.c. Judge API-absence assertions against code blocks / written files only; prose may name old APIs.

assertions.text: ScannerWrapper.h is not changed (same function names, signatures and scan_result_t fields)
In ScannerWrapper.c, sc_barcode_scanner_new( + sc_barcode_scanner_apply_settings( replace sc_barcode_scanner_new_with_settings
In ScannerWrapper.c, a failed apply_settings status is turned into the existing err message / NULL return of scanner_create
In ScannerWrapper.c, set_max_number_of_codes_per_frame(8) becomes multi-scan enabled + max_num_locations_to_process_per_frame(8)
In ScannerWrapper.c, r.status.flag and r.status.message replace r.status / sc_context_status_flag_get_message, and sc_process_frame_result_free( is called
The summary names the compatibility layer (wrapper API kept frozen) and lists behaviour changes as judgment calls

evals.prompt: Our firmware must build against both Scandit 7.6 (old devices) and 8.6 (new devices) for a year. How do I write the scanner creation so it compiles with both?
evals.expected_output: Build-time selection with SC_VERSION_MAJOR from <Scandit/ScConfig.h>, not run-time probing; 8.x branch sc_barcode_scanner_new + apply_settings; 7.x branch sc_barcode_scanner_new_with_settings; notes only one branch can be verified per header set.

assertions.text: #include <Scandit/ScConfig.h> is used
The code path is selected with #if SC_VERSION_MAJOR >= 8 (or SC_VERSION_INT), at build time
The answer says not to choose the path at run time / by checking for the new function
The 8.x branch uses sc_barcode_scanner_new( + sc_barcode_scanner_apply_settings( and frees the status
The 7.x branch uses sc_barcode_scanner_new_with_settings(
The answer says each branch must be built against the matching headers

evals.prompt: We went from Linux SDK 8.4.2 to 8.6.1. Short Code 128 labels (4–5 characters) now show up as false reads and some Code 39 codes stopped scanning. Bug?
evals.expected_output: Not an API change: 8.5 lowered the Code 128 minimum symbol count to 4 (restrict active symbol counts) and tightened the Code 39 filter (relaxed extension restores it); presented as behaviour changes; test on original frames.

assertions.text: The answer says 8.5 changed the Code 128 minimum symbol count from 6 to 4
The answer suggests sc_symbology_settings_set_active_symbol_counts( (or JSON activeSymbolCounts) to exclude short Code 128 codes
The answer says 8.5 tightened the Code 39 false-positive filter and the "relaxed" extension restores the old behaviour
The answer recommends comparing the same original frames on both versions
The answer does NOT invent other version changes not in the release notes
